# Markitai: Agent guide

> Plain Markdown for AI assistants, included in CLI archives for offline use.

Markitai converts local documents, images and HTTP(S) pages to Markdown and
assets. The CLI needs no Python, Node.js or Go runtime. Recognized formats have
fidelity limits; see [Quick start](docs/quickstart.md) for formats and backends.

## Inputs and state

Use the caller's authorized inputs, an absolute executable path and a specific
output directory. Set `MARKITAI_HOME` to isolate state instead of the default
`~/.markitai`. Configuration also comes from the working directory and
environment; control those when isolation matters.

For local document text without OCR, model enhancement or third-party services:

```sh
markitai /absolute/path/report.docx -o /absolute/path/output -b native --no-llm --no-ocr --no-remote-fetch --json
```

Windows uses `markitai.exe` and Windows absolute paths. Archives also provide
`mkai` and `markitai-mcp` (`.exe` on Windows). An Agent may not inherit an
interactive shell's PATH; configure the executable's full path.

## CLI machine output

`--json` requires `-o` and writes a result envelope to stdout; diagnostics go
to stderr. Without either option, stdout is Markdown and asset links can be
persistent absolute `file://` URIs under Markitai state.

Read top-level `ok` / `error` and each item's `status`, `skip_reason`, output
paths and warnings. Empty stdout does not establish success. A standalone
image without OCR or LLM extraction is skipped as `image_only`.

Exit codes are 0 for success or supported skips, 1 for a single failure,
2 for invalid arguments or a still-pending provider batch, and 10 for batch
item failures. Argument errors can precede JSON creation: inspect stderr too.
Reports under `output/.markitai/reports/` supplement the envelope.

Choose a conflict policy for retries; the default is `rename`. `--pure`
suppresses generated frontmatter; it does not disable configured model calls.
Use `--no-llm` to disable model processing. Directory and `.urls` batches support
`--resume` on macOS, Linux and Windows; single inputs do not.
Final Markdown omits PDF page and slide-number comments by default; `--page-markers`
keeps them, and the equivalent configuration is `output.page_markers=true`.
See [CLI](docs/cli.md) for options and the complete envelope.

## MCP

Start `markitai mcp` or `markitai-mcp` over stdio (`.exe` on Windows), using an
absolute executable path and isolated state when needed. Protocol messages
use stdout, diagnostics use stderr; there is no HTTP MCP endpoint.

- `convert_document`: an absolute local `path` (`~` is expanded). Ordinary directories are not documents; modern `.numbers` packages are.
- `convert_url`: an HTTP(S) URL; may use the network or browser.
- `batch_convert`: a nonempty list of paths and/or URLs; returns a job ID.
- `job_status`: poll in the same server process until `completed` or `cancelled`, then inspect individual failures. A completed job can contain failed items.

Single-input tools accept `output_dir`, `llm`, `ocr`, `screenshot`, `alt`,
`desc` and `profile`. Omitted/null feature flags follow configuration; use
explicit false to disable them. `output_dir` must be absolute; omitted, null
or empty creates a retained temporary directory. Keep it while using assets
and delete it when finished, including after server shutdown.

Results include `structuredContent` and a JSON text block. When `truncated`
is true, read `markdown_file` for the complete output. Expected conversion
errors carry `isError: true`; do not parse progress text as tool results.
[MCP](docs/mcp.md) documents schemas and host configuration.

## Offline and optional components

Local text conversion needs no provider access. macOS defaults to Vision OCR;
Windows/Linux use local Paddle and built-in hayro PDF rendering. Paddle models
are separate downloads. `markitai doctor --json` checks readiness;
`doctor --fix` can download missing models and repair safely managed corrupt
models. Prepare them before going offline; never bypass an unsafe-path error.

HEIF/HEIC decodes on every platform (macOS ImageIO, a built-in pure-Rust decoder
on Windows/Linux); AVIF decoding uses macOS ImageIO and is unsupported on
Windows/Linux.
JavaScript pages and browser screenshots need Chrome/Chromium. Office page
images and OCR supplements need LibreOffice; native text readers do not.
Spreadsheet screenshots include hidden and empty sheets, one page per sheet,
ignoring print areas and manual pagination. Oversized sheets fail the pixel
budget rather than being cropped. Numbers text extraction is supported;
Numbers screenshots are not.

Model enhancement can send content to configured providers or subscription
runtimes. `--no-llm` disables that step. `--no-remote-fetch` blocks third-party
fetch services, not direct HTTP(S) downloads or browser requests. Offline work
must also avoid URLs, remote resources and unprepared components.

Bindings need their language runtimes. Windows Go/cgo packages are outside
the supported delivery scope; self-contained Go packages target macOS arm64
and Linux x86-64 (glibc).

## Workbench and HTTP callers

`markitai serve` listens on loopback by default. Its printed browser URL holds
the access token in a fragment. With authentication enabled, API callers need
the token even locally; one-use tickets can authorize designated downloads.
Keep token-bearing URLs out of shared logs. CLI and MCP do not need this service.

Cloudflare needs server configuration and explicit user consent for every
create, retry or enhancement request. Select its strategy or backend and set
`remote_processing: "cloudflare"` in that request's options. `Item.options`
and history are saved choices, not consent. Server hard-off and `never`
policy still apply; credentials and endpoints stay on the server.

Readiness checks local configuration, not cloud permissions or quota. A request
marker does not prove cloud execution. External charges are excluded from the
LLM subtotal; inspect cost warnings before interpreting zero as free.

## Further documentation

[README](README.md), [quick start](docs/quickstart.md), [CLI](docs/cli.md) and
[MCP](docs/mcp.md) are included offline. The [index](docs/index.md) links other
guides, including the full HTTP contract, which require the repository checkout.
